learn: Common fitness tests include the PACER (cardio), push-ups and curl-ups (muscular), and sit-and-reach (flexibility).
Tests measure your current level so you can track progress.
Healthy fitness zones depend on age, not on comparing to classmates.
lessons.try: Record your results in three fitness tests.

learn: SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound.
"Get fitter" is vague; "Run a mile in under 10 minutes by March" is SMART.
Break big goals into weekly steps.
check: Run a mile in under 10 minutes by March
The T in SMART stands for...
Big goals should be broken into...
lessons.try: Write a SMART fitness goal and weekly steps.

learn: Keep a fitness log of activities, time and how you felt.
Review progress every few weeks and adjust your plan.
Celebrate improvement, not perfection.
lessons.try: Keep a fitness log for two weeks.

learn: Major muscles include the biceps, triceps, quadriceps, hamstrings, abdominals, deltoids and glutes.
Muscles work in pairs: when the biceps contracts, the triceps relaxes.
Training all groups keeps the body balanced.
check: The front of the thigh is the...
lessons.try: Name the muscle used in five different exercises.

learn: Bodyweight exercises use your own weight: push-ups, squats, lunges, planks.
Good form matters more than speed or number.
Teens should focus on technique and light resistance, with adult supervision for weights.
lessons.try: Do a circuit of four bodyweight exercises with good form.

learn: Strength is built with fewer repetitions against more resistance.
Endurance is built with more repetitions against less resistance.
Rest days let muscles recover and grow stronger.
lessons.try: Plan a week with strength days, endurance days and rest.

units.t: Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Target Heart Rate

learn: Estimated maximum heart rate is 220 minus your age.
For a 12-year-old, that's about 208 beats per minute.
This is an estimate; individuals vary.
lessons.try: Calculate your estimated maximum heart rate.

learn: The target zone for improving fitness is about 60-85% of maximum heart rate.
For a max of 208, that's roughly 125-177 beats per minute.
Check your pulse during exercise to stay in the zone.
check: The target zone is about ___ of max heart rate.
lessons.try: Exercise for ten minutes and check whether you are in your zone.

learn: Aerobic exercise uses oxygen for steady activity: jogging, swimming.
Anaerobic exercise is short, intense bursts: sprinting, jumping.
Both are important for overall fitness.
lessons.try: Do a workout mixing steady jogging and short sprints.

learn: Volleyball skills include the bump (forearm pass), set and serve.
Badminton uses a shuttlecock and quick wrist movements.
Strategy: hit to open spaces and recover to base position.
check: The forearm pass in volleyball is the...
lessons.try: Rally a volleyball with a partner using bumps and sets.

learn: Wall games include handball and squash, where players hit a ball against a wall.
Players alternate shots and aim to make returns difficult.
Watch the ball and move your feet early.
check: In wall games, the ball is hit against a...
lessons.try: Play a wall-ball game with a partner.

learn: Softball, baseball and cricket are striking and fielding games.
Batters strike and run; fielders catch and throw to get them out.
Communication ("mine!") prevents collisions.
lessons.try: Practise catching and throwing with a partner at increasing distances.

learn: Teens need more energy as they grow and stay active.
Calories measure energy in food.
Balance energy from food with energy used in activity.
lessons.try: Estimate how much activity you do daily.

learn: Eat carbohydrates (whole grains, fruit) for energy before exercise.
Protein after exercise helps muscles recover.
Drink water throughout the day; sports drinks are only needed for long, intense activity.
lessons.try: Plan a pre-game snack and a recovery meal.

learn: Avoid skipping meals, especially breakfast.
Limit sugary drinks and highly processed snacks.
Every body is different; healthy bodies come in many shapes and sizes.
lessons.try: Write three positive things your body can do.

learn: Self-esteem is how you value yourself.
Resilience is the ability to bounce back from setbacks.
A growth mindset sees mistakes as chances to learn.
check: A growth mindset sees mistakes as...
lessons.try: Write about a time you overcame a challenge.

learn: Stressors for teens include school, friendships and family changes.
Healthy strategies: exercise, time management, breathing, hobbies, talking to someone.
Unhealthy strategies like isolating or ignoring problems make stress worse.
check: Which is a healthy stress strategy?
lessons.try: Make a personal stress-management plan.

learn: Signs someone may need help: long-lasting sadness, withdrawing, changes in sleep or eating.
Tell a trusted adult if you or a friend is struggling.
Counsellors and helplines provide support.
check: Long-lasting sadness is a sign to...
If a friend is struggling, tell...
lessons.try: Find your school counsellor's name and office.

learn: Tobacco and most vapes contain nicotine, a highly addictive drug.
Nicotine harms the developing teen brain, affecting attention and learning.
Vaping can damage the lungs; secondhand smoke harms others.
lessons.try: Make a poster about the facts of vaping.

learn: Alcohol slows the brain and body, affecting judgment, coordination and reaction time.
Teen brains are still developing, so alcohol is especially harmful.
It is illegal for anyone under 21 to buy alcohol in the United States.
check: In the US, the legal age to buy alcohol is...
lessons.try: Discuss how alcohol affects decisions and safety.

learn: Refusal skills: say "no" clearly, give a reason, suggest another activity, leave if needed.
Choose friends who respect your decisions.
Talk to a trusted adult if you feel pressured.
lessons.try: Role-play refusing an offer of a vape.

learn: Healthy relationships involve respect, trust, honesty and communication.
Warning signs of unhealthy relationships: jealousy, control, put-downs, pressure.
Everyone deserves to feel safe and respected.
lessons.try: Make a chart of healthy and unhealthy behaviours.

learn: Passive: not standing up for yourself. Aggressive: attacking others.
Assertive: expressing your needs clearly and respectfully.
Assertive communication uses "I" statements.
check: Not standing up for yourself is...
lessons.try: Rewrite an aggressive statement as an assertive one.

learn: Steps: stay calm, listen, state your view, brainstorm solutions, agree on one.
Compromise means each side gives a little.
Walk away and get help if a conflict becomes unsafe.
check: The first step in resolving conflict is to...
lessons.try: Role-play resolving a disagreement over a group project.

learn: Check the scene is safe, check the person, call for help, then care.
In the US, call 911; give your location and what happened.
Do not move someone with a possible neck or back injury.
check: First, check that the scene is...
With a possible neck injury, you should...
lessons.try: Practise what you would say on an emergency call.

learn: Cuts: apply pressure with a clean cloth, then clean and cover.
Burns: cool under running water for 10-20 minutes; don't use ice or butter.
Nosebleeds: lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose.
lessons.try: Make a first-aid card for your backpack.

learn: Signs of choking: can't speak, cough or breathe, hands at throat.
Abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich manoeuvre) can clear the airway; take a certified course to learn properly.
CPR and AEDs help someone whose heart has stopped; trained adults should lead.
check: To learn CPR properly, take a...
lessons.try: Find where the nearest AED is in your school.

learn: Lifetime activities include walking, cycling, swimming, tennis, golf, dance and yoga.
Choose activities you enjoy and can do with others.
Variety prevents boredom and overuse injuries.
lessons.try: Try a new lifetime activity and rate it.

learn: Hiking, kayaking, rock climbing and camping build fitness and confidence.
Plan, prepare and follow safety rules.
Respect nature: Leave No Trace.
lessons.try: Plan a safe outdoor day with a checklist.

learn: Adults should get at least 150 minutes of moderate activity a week.
Active lifestyles lower the risk of heart disease, diabetes and depression.
Habits formed now last a lifetime.
check: Adults need at least ___ minutes of moderate activity weekly.
lessons.try: Write a letter to your future self about staying active.
